# API Requirements Checklist: Endpoints de métricas de negocio

**Purpose**: Evaluar claridad, completitud y consistencia de los requisitos de métricas de negocio y sus contratos.
**Created**: 2026-11-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the historical and current metric sources, time boundaries, and distinct purposes explicitly specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, FR-002]
- [x] CHK002 Are all five business aggregates and their contribution rules defined for both views, including zero-activity responses? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-005]
- [x] CHK003 Are authentication and access requirements stated consistently for both endpoints, including the absence of a role requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK004 Are the required OpenAPI documentation elements for each endpoint identified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Clarity and Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK005 Are the JSON field names, types, units, and timestamp format unambiguous and identical for both endpoints? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK006 Can the rule for classifying each financial record as a purchase or sale be applied without double-counting or ambiguity? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK007 Are the event-counting boundaries clear for completed, rejected, failed, and multi-operation requests? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK008 Can the success criteria objectively establish response-contract parity and source-aligned aggregate values? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001–SC-003]

## Requirement Consistency and Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK009 Are the historical and process-local definitions consistent across user scenarios, edge cases, functional requirements, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §US1–US2, Edge Cases, FR-001–FR-005, SC-001–SC-003]
- [x] CHK010 Are cancellation requirements consistent in distinguishing `CANCELLED` from `EXPIRED` and excluding financial movements caused solely by cancellation? [Consistency, Spec §US1, Edge Cases, FR-005]
- [x] CHK011 Are unauthenticated access, authenticated access, and prohibited personal or high-cardinality data exposure all covered by requirements and measurable outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §US3, FR-006–FR-007, SC-004]
- [x] CHK012 Are empty history, process restart, and a request completing multiple operations addressed as explicit scenarios or boundary conditions? [Coverage, Spec §US1–US2, Edge Cases]

## Scope, Dependencies, and Assumptions

- [x] CHK013 Are exclusions for technical metrics, monitoring deployment, persisted-history replacement, and individual breakdowns explicit and consistent? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK014 Are assumptions about existing authentication, Micrometer counters, and the centesimal credit unit traceable to the requirements they constrain? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline; link to relevant resources or documentation.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
